title: The youth department's grants by service area: money, participants and cost
question: How much did the Department of Children, Youth and Their Families grant in each service area, how much was spent, and how many young people took part?
finding: The year-end reports show $108.4 million granted in 2024-25 and $110.0 million in 2025-26 across 8 service areas (255 programs), with $104.7 million and $104.1 million spent. The sharpest change is in Justice Services: participant service days fell from 194,889 to 36,382 (-81%) while spending was $13.1 million in both years and unique participants went from 1,179 to 1,126; spending per participant day rose from $67.43 to $359.89. Family Empowerment grants rose from $6.2 million to $6.6 million while spending fell from $5.9 million to $5.8 million (13% of the grant unspent).
how: Read from the department's published year-end report for each service area (files without the '24' prefix are 2025-26, files with it 2024-25, as each report's heading says). Grants and spending are the sum of the strategy table; participants are the report's unique participants; participant service days are its total days of participation. Cost per participant is spending over unique participants.
limits: Unique participants leave out young people reported only in aggregate, so cost per participant is overstated where aggregate reporting is common; participant days include them. A fall in days can come from a change in how programs report (how days are counted, or a program that stopped or moved to another strategy) rather than fewer services; the report gives no reason. The service-area reports name no grantee; the department's grantee pages, saved on 20 November 2026, trace most of the Justice Services fall to one program's aggregate count (screen youth_records.justice-days-traced).
